From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Review of the Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Bottom line:** The Seller's package departs from our playbook on almost every material point. Taken together, the changes would sharply reduce the Seller's real exposure. They do this by lowering the cap, raising the thresholds, shortening the claims period, folding Title into the general regime, and stripping the fraud carve-out through "all Claims" wording. They also gut the warranties through general disclosure and a broad buyer-knowledge bar. On top of that, the completion-critical items (Bluefen, Riverlark and the bonuses) are left open.

## A preliminary point: the "FINAL" framing

The preamble says these positions "were settled at principal level by both deal teams" and are "FINAL and not intended to be re-opened." We should not accept that.

- **No authority from our side.** Our playbook records that Amelia Frost has given no written authority for the 20% cap or the 18-month period. Nothing in the Seller's papers is evidence of any agreement by Wattlebridge.
- **Unverified market claims.** The statements about market norms (10–20% caps, baskets of about 1%, 12–18 months, buyer-knowledge qualifiers) are the Seller's advocacy. They are not agreed terms, and they do not change our mandate.
- **Next step.** The deal team should confirm internally that Amelia has not agreed anything at principal level. Our mark-up should say expressly that all positions remain open.

## 1. Liability regime

| Issue | Seller position | Playbook | Assessment / pushback |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Cap (cl 12.1)** | 20% / AUD 4.8m | 25% / AUD 6.0m. 20% is a fallback only with Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying this draft. | **Reject.** Mark up to 25% / AUD 6.0m. Do not concede 20% unless written authority is obtained for this specific draft. |
| **De minimis (cl 12.2)** | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 | **Reject.** At five times our level, it would exclude many real SaaS warranty claims. |
| **Basket (cl 12.2)** | AUD 250,000, excess only | AUD 50,000, first-dollar recovery once exceeded | **Reject both elements.** The "excess only" mechanism means AUD 250k of loss is never recoverable. Revert to AUD 50k on a tipping basis. |
| **Claims period (cl 12.3)** | 18 months | 24 months. 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia's written approval. | **Reject.** Revert to 24 months. |
| **"All Claims" limitation (cl 12.3/13)** | Any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise | Title/Tax/IP/payment/covenant categories kept separate, with no hidden override | **Reject.** This is a drafting trap. It would silently pull fundamental claims, indemnities, covenant claims and price/payment obligations under the general caps and time limits. Limitations should apply only to "General Warranty Claims", as expressly defined. |

## 2. Fundamental and Title warranties

The Seller wants capacity and title warranties under the general caps and time limits "for administrative simplicity." **Reject this outright.** These warranties go to the existence of what we are buying.

Our playbook position is a separate regime:
- a cap of 100% of price;
- a claims period of at least six years;
- no general basket, de minimis or knowledge bar.

## 3. Fraud carve-out (cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5)

The Seller wants the limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions to apply to "all Claims of any nature." As drafted, this purports to cap or exclude liability for fraud. **This is non-negotiable for us.**

- Insert an express carve-out for fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct.
- The carve-out must apply to all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions, to the maximum extent enforceable.
- No deal team member has authority to waive this.
- Even if a court might not enforce a fraud exclusion, we should not let the drafting invite the argument.

## 4. Disclosure (Schedule 7 and Disclosure Letter cl 1)

- **cl 1.1 (whole data room).** This discloses "every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to" in the data room. That is the whole-data-room disclosure our playbook rejects. "Referred to" is even wider, because it would capture documents that are mentioned but not provided. **Delete.** Disclosure should be limited to the specific disclosures in the letter, made fairly and with enough detail for the Buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter.
- **cl 1.2 (Accounts, registers, public records).** These are deemed disclosures. **Delete.** At most, the Accounts could be accepted against specific warranties where they are expressly identified.
- **Numbering gap.** The letter jumps from 1.2 to 1.4, so clause 1.3 is missing. Ask the Seller to confirm whether text was removed, and make sure nothing is incorporated by reference.
- **cl 1.4 (no admission).** A no-admission clause is common and acceptable in principle. However, it must not operate to deny that the Bluefen consent, the Riverlark repayment and discharge, or the bonuses are completion requirements. The SPA conditions should govern those.
- **Staleness.** The data room cut-off is 22 September 2026, about six weeks before today (4 November 2026). Require bring-down disclosure, updated as close to signing and Completion as possible, with no new general disclosures allowed.

## 5. Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3)

This bars claims for anything known to the Buyer or its advisers, including anything "discoverable from the data room or public records." It is a blanket constructive-knowledge exclusion and goes further than even general disclosure. **Delete.**

If any knowledge qualifier survives, it must:
- be limited to the actual knowledge of named Buyer deal-team individuals;
- never apply to title, capacity, fraud or any specific indemnity.

We should also seek **Seller-knowledge** qualifiers in the warranties. These should refer to named Seller knowledge persons and include a reasonable-enquiry obligation.

## 6. Completion-critical items

### Bluefen (cl 3 / 6.3)

Bluefen is about 30% of revenue (about AUD 3.6m FY26). Under DD-002 cl 11.2–11.3, its consent carries conditions. The Seller offers only "reasonable endeavours" and treats the condition as satisfied when the written consent is delivered. Its own Disclosure Letter (cl 2) confirms that neither a final consent nor evidence that the conditions are satisfied has been provided.

**Push back:**
- The Completion condition should require an effective, unconditional written consent from Bluefen.
- It should also require evidence, satisfactory to the Buyer, that every 11.3 condition is satisfied before Completion.
- The condition should be waivable by the Buyer only.
- Reasonable endeavours alone is not enough for a customer of this size.
- Consider a Buyer termination right, or price protection, if the consent is not obtained by the long-stop date.

### Riverlark (cl 2 / 7)

About AUD 3.2m is outstanding. The facility contains change-control (8.1) and discharge (9.2) provisions. The Seller offers a "release following Completion." The Disclosure Letter (cl 3) confirms there has been no repayment and no discharge.

**Push back:**
- Obtain a current payout letter.
- Repay the facility directly from Completion funds, as a funds-flow line.
- Deliver effective security releases (including PPSR releases and any deed of release) at Completion, consistent with the debt-free/cash-free basis.
- A post-completion release is acceptable only with an irrevocable bank undertaking **and** Amelia Frost's approval. Neither is offered.
- Note the change-control clause (8.1). Completion without repayment could trigger a default.

### Employee bonuses (DD-005) and the funds flow

The Seller states that the AUD 420,000 in bonuses "are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised." In practice the Company, which we will own, is likely to be the payer. If so, the cost would fall on us after Completion, together with payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs. The disclosure does not say whether those on-costs apply.

**Push back:** Include the AUD 420,000 and all triggered on-costs as either:
- a specific funds-flow deduction or Debt-like item; or
- an obligation the Seller funds, backed by an indemnity.

The funds flow must not silently exclude them. Ask the Seller to confirm the on-cost position.

## 7. Specific matters

- **Ironquay IP (cl 11.1).** The indemnity covers only the SOW3 payment. Under DD-004 cl 7.3, transfer of the SOW3 Project Materials depends on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. There is no receipt and no confirmatory assignment.
  - Broaden the indemnity to cover any loss from failure of IP to vest, third-party IP claims, and Ironquay asserting rights. Keep the SOW3 cure route.
  - Seek a confirmatory assignment as a Completion deliverable, or payment plus proof of receipt.
  - The DD-010 figure of AUD 180,000 is not independently verified. Do not treat it as a confirmed debt or a confirmed cap in either direction.
- **DD-006 export/privacy incident (cl 4.6 / Sch 6).** The Seller calls this "preliminary" and "not expected to be material." That is the Seller's characterisation, and nothing establishes materiality either way. The facts are that about 1,240 records may have been sent to an unintended external address, and access, scope and any notification duty are unresolved.
  - Require preservation of logs.
  - Require a proper investigation, which could be independent.
  - Require regular updates before Completion, with Buyer consultation rights on any notification decisions.
  - Seek a specific indemnity or warranty protection for loss arising from the incident.
  - Do not assert a confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand.
- **Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000).** The Seller asserts these are ordinary-course costs. The disclosure itself does not say whether each renewal is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary-course.
  - Request the facts on timing, terminability, accrual and whether the renewals were approved under conduct-of-business covenants.
  - Do not assume a Debt classification or a price deduction at this stage. Hold the position open pending that analysis.
- **Office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009).** The disclosure says the lease needs notification and the Mossvale clause restricts assignment, but neither is said to require consent to a share sale. Have our own counsel confirm that reading of the underlying documents. Make lease notification a Seller obligation or Completion deliverable where appropriate.

## 8. Tax, IP and Title

- **Tax and IP.** The Seller considers these "settled under the general regime." On our playbook they remain **OPEN**. Do not accept that they are resolved. Keep them as separate categories, outside the general cap, basket and time limits as our final terms will provide. Do not assume unlimited liability.
- **Title.** The DD-012 share register is a supplied internal source. Disclosure Letter cl 10 itself says the Buyer has not verified title. Require independent evidence:
  - an ASIC company extract consistent with the register;
  - a PPSR search, plus confirmation of no encumbrances (the Riverlark security is relevant here);
  - share certificates;
  - board and shareholder authorisations;
  - confirmation of no options or other rights over the shares;
  - capacity and authority evidence for Harbourglass.

## Summary of recommendations

1. **Reject the "FINAL / settled at principal level" framing.** Confirm internally that Amelia Frost has given no authority, and state in the mark-up that all points are open.
2. **Cap:** 25% / AUD 6.0m. 20% only with Amelia's written authority for this draft.
3. **Thresholds:** de minimis AUD 5,000, and an AUD 50,000 basket that tips to first-dollar recovery.
4. **Claims period:** 24 months.
5. **Fundamental/Title regime:** separate, with a 100% cap, at least six years, and no basket, de minimis or knowledge bar.
6. **Fraud carve-out:** fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of everything. Non-negotiable.
7. **"All Claims" wording:** delete it in cl 12.3/13, 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5. Limitations should apply to defined General Warranty Claims only.
8. **Disclosure:** specific fair disclosure only. Delete 1.1 and 1.2, query the missing 1.3, and require bring-down disclosure.
9. **Buyer knowledge:** delete cl 8.3. Add Seller-knowledge persons with reasonable enquiry.
10. **Bluefen:** effective consent plus evidence that the 11.3 conditions are satisfied, as a Buyer-only waivable condition precedent.
11. **Riverlark:** payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds and releases at Completion. Any post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia's approval.
12. **Bonuses:** AUD 420k plus on-costs as a funds-flow line or Seller-funded with an indemnity.
13. **Ironquay:** broaden the indemnity, preserve the SOW3 cure, and seek a confirmatory assignment. Treat the AUD 180k as unverified.
14. **DD-006:** preservation, investigation, updates and indemnity protection. Make no assumption of breach, harm or notification duty.
15. **Sandbar:** request facts. No automatic Debt classification or deduction.
16. **Tax/IP:** expressly open and kept separate.
17. **Title:** independent verification beyond DD-012.

Shall I turn this into a mark-up issues list or draft rider clauses for the cap, the fraud carve-out and the disclosure provisions?
